history.summary: Shiva shrine on the northern side of the Jagannath Temple, by the Markandeya Tank. Tradition says sage Markandeya meditated and installed a Shivalinga here after Shiva saved him from the sea; the present temple was built under the Ganga dynasty around the 12th century. It is counted among the Pancha Tirthas (five pilgrimage sites) of Puri and the Pancha Pandava Shiva temples of Puri (associated with Arjuna). The large Markandeya Tank beside it is used for ritual bathing, Pinda Dana and Mundan ceremonies.

name: Markandeshwar Temple
town_description: Puri is a coastal pilgrim city in Odisha, famed for the Jagannath Temple, one of the four Char Dham of Hinduism. It draws millions of pilgrims and tourists each year, especially during the annual Rath Yatra, and is known for its long golden beach. Puri lies about 60 km south of Bhubaneswar and is well connected by rail and road.
